Passage from the lesson 'Python - Chapter 9: Functions (Comprehensive)':
Every non-trivial program repeats work: the same calculation, the same check, the same sequence of steps. Copying that code everywhere makes programs long, hard to read, and dangerous to change - fix a bug in one copy and the other copies still break. A function packages a piece of behaviour under a name so you write it once, give it a clear label, and reuse it everywhere. Functions are the first and most important tool for managing complexity: they let you think in terms of "what" (the name and purpose) instead of "how" (the lines of code). Three big wins follow: (1) you stop repeating yourself (the "DRY" principle), (2) you can name an idea, which makes code self-documenting, and (3) you can test a small piece in isolation instead of running the whole program.

Explain 'Why Functions Exist' using only this passage.

Every non-trivial program repeats work: the same calculation, the same check, the same sequence of steps. Copying that code everywhere makes programs long, hard to read, and dangerous to change - fix a bug in one copy and the other copies still break. A function packages a piece of behaviour under a name so you write it once, give it a clear label, and reuse it everywhere. Functions are the first and most important tool for managing complexity: they let you think in terms of "what" (the name and purpose) instead of "how" (the lines of code). Three big wins follow: (1) you stop repeating yourself (the "DRY" principle), (2) you can name an idea, which makes code self-documenting, and (3) you can test a small piece in isolation instead of running the whole program.

A system of linear equations is a collection of equations that must all be satisfied simultaneously. A system can have exactly one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solution at all. Geometric intuition: each equation represents a line (in 2D) or a plane (in 3D), and solutions are their intersections.

Passage from the lesson 'Calculus I':
The limit of a function f(x) as x approaches a is the value f(x) gets closer and closer to, even if f(a) itself is undefined. We write this as lim_{x→a} f(x) = L. Limits let us talk rigorously about instantaneous rates and areas under curves.

instruction:
Passage from the lesson 'Python - Chapter 9: Functions (Comprehensive)':
A function definition has five parts: the def keyword, a name, a parenthesised parameter list, a colon, and an indented body. Indentation is not cosmetic in Python - it is how the language knows which lines belong to the function. def greet(name): message = "Hello, " + name return message Here `def` starts the definition, `greet` is the name, `name` is a parameter, the colon ends the header, and the two indented lines are the body. The body does not run when Python reads the definition; it runs only when the function is called. Defining a function is like writing a recipe; calling it is cooking.

Explain 'The Anatomy of a Function' using only this passage.
